assets.title: 8 Hours on Low, One Bag of Dried Beans, 8 Bowls of Dinner
assets.description: Two pounds of dried pinto beans, a pound of smoked sausage, and 8 to 10 hours on low. That's dinner for 8 out of one slow cooker, at about 420 calories a bowl. Cheap crockpot meals for large families work because the crockpot doesn't care that the beans came from a bag instead of a can.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading 8 hours on low, one bag of dried beans, 8 bowls of dinner, over a line about cheap crockpot meals for large families.

assets.title: Six Eggs, Six Breakfast Burritos, Three Months in the Freezer
assets.description: Six eggs across six burritos, plus a can of black beans and a cup of shredded cheese doing the rest of the work. These high protein breakfast burritos hold up for about 3 months in the freezer. Vegetarian, roughly 380 calories each, and no drive-thru involved.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading six eggs, six breakfast burritos, three months in the freezer.

assets.title: Put the Snack Bin at Eye Level. Visibility Is Half the Battle
assets.description: A clear bin on the middle shelf beats the bottom crisper every time, because things go to the crisper to die. When you open the door it should be the first thing you see. That's the entire idea behind a grab and go snack drawer.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading put the snack bin at eye level, visibility is half the battle.

assets.title: Aim for 8 to 10 Grams of Fiber Before Noon
assets.description: You don't need to hit the whole day's fiber at breakfast. Roughly 8 to 10 grams in the morning already puts you ahead of most muffin and latte routines. Stack any two easy high fiber breakfast foods and you're there before you've properly woken up.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading aim for 8 to 10 grams of fiber before noon.

assets.board: Grocery Budget Tips and Shopping Lists
assets.title: USDA Puts One Adult at $303 to $381 a Month for Food at Home
assets.description: The thrifty benchmark works out to about $303 a month for a woman living alone and $381 for a man, using May 2026 prices. That range already includes the 20 percent USDA adds for one person households. Use it as a shape to compare your own grocery spending against, not as a quote.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading USDA puts one adult at $303 to $381 a month for food at home.
assets.release_gate: Verify the live article's USDA month and one-person figures on release day.

assets.board: Sourdough Discard Recipes and Easy Bread
assets.title: Crusty Homemade Bread Lives on the Counter, Cut Side Down
assets.description: A crackly crust and a plastic bag are enemies. For the first day or two, set the loaf cut side down on a wooden surface or in a paper bag and leave it alone. Storing homemade bread is mostly about matching the method to the crust you worked for.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading crusty homemade bread lives on the counter, cut side down.

assets.board: How to Cook Chicken, Pork and Beef
assets.title: How to Cook Chicken Breast: Four to Six Minutes a Side, Pulled at 165F
assets.description: The best way to cook chicken breast in a skillet is four to six minutes per side over real heat, pulled at an internal temperature of 165F. Put the thermometer into the thickest part from the side, not from the top, or you'll read the hot pan instead. Under 25 minutes from fridge to fork.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading four to six minutes a side, and a thermometer at 165F.
assets.release_gate: Verify the live article's timing and temperature guidance on release day.

assets.title: The Cabbage Slaw Is the Whole Point of a Fish Taco
assets.description: Mayonnaise, lime juice and a minced chipotle in adobo, tossed through two cups of shredded cabbage. That homemade dressing is what makes a fish taco feel like a full plate instead of fish in a tortilla. Make the slaw first and let it sit.
assets.alt_text: Cream text pin reading the cabbage slaw is the whole point, the fish is incidental.

channels.title: We Ranked 53 Foods by Fiber per Dollar
channels.script: We priced 53 foods by grams of fiber per dollar. Whole wheat flour came first in this July 2026 snapshot at 77.8 grams per dollar. Dry split peas, pinto beans, black beans, and popcorn kernels filled the next seats. The produce aisle was invited. It just didn't win the spreadsheet. Full CSV and method at daily-life-hacks.com.

channels.title: I priced 53 foods by grams of fiber per dollar. The dry-goods aisle was rude about it.
channels.initial_link_policy: No link in the initial post.
channels.body_markdown:
Disclosure: I run Daily Life Hacks, and this is from a grocery-price dataset I built.

I compared 53 foods using package price, package weight, edible fraction, and USDA fiber per 100 grams. This was a July 2026 US price snapshot, so it isn't a promise about your store.

| Rank | Food | Fiber per dollar |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | Whole wheat flour | 77.8 g |
| 2 | Green split peas, dry | 71.0 g |
| 3 | Pinto beans, dry | 70.8 g |
| 4 | Black beans, dry | 58.1 g |
| 5 | Popcorn kernels | 57.7 g |

The useful part wasn't "beans are cheap." Civilization had that scoop. It was seeing how much package size, edible waste, and the actual shelf price changed the order.

If the community wants it and the rules allow it, I'll add the full CSV and method in a comment. Otherwise, the table can stay here and earn its keep.
